html:
Potawatomi-Shawnee (Oklahoma) marks the shared lands of the Citizen Potawatomi Nation and the Absentee Shawnee Tribe in central Oklahoma, around the towns of Shawnee and Tecumseh.

The Potawatomi came from the Great Lakes. In 1838 many were forced from Indiana to Kansas on the Trail of Death. A group that took United States citizenship under an 1861 treaty moved on to Indian Territory in the 1870s, which is why they are called the Citizen Potawatomi.

The Absentee Shawnee were Shawnee who had left the main body and lived in Texas and then on the Canadian River in Indian Territory, away, or absent, from the Shawnee reserve in Kansas. In 1891 their shared reservation was split into allotments and opened to settlers. The Kickapoo live just to the north.
sum: Potawatomi-Shawnee (Oklahoma) marks the shared lands of the Citizen Potawatomi Nation and the Absentee Shawnee Tribe in central Oklahoma, around the towns of Shawnee and Tecumseh.
